record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not

claims.claim: Morphine, a close morphinan analog, had a mean oral bioavailability of 29.2 ± 7.2% after oral tablet versus IV dosing in fasted healthy volunteers, which is above the 20% threshold.

Ethylmorphine, another structurally related morphinan, showed absolute oral bioavailability of 28% in a subject receiving both oral and IV doses, and a median systemic availability of 0.74 by metabolite recovery.
Codeine sulfate, a related morphinan, had oral bioavailability of 80.5% in healthy subjects, further supporting high oral availability in this structural class.

evidence_gaps: No direct oral bioavailability measurement for the query molecule is present in the supplied records.
The query differs from the closest analogs by N-allyl substitution, a 6-keto group, and a 14-hydroxy group, which may alter first-pass metabolism but are not directly quantified here.
No query-specific metabolism, clearance, or efflux data are available.
